narrative.overview: Lotus Quant is a quiet professional interface built around one recurring act: placing attention onto a complicated portfolio signal. The optical risk field visualizes exposure as coherent channels and turns the pointer into a movable analytical lens. Graphite type carries authority; cobalt marks analytical action; vermilion identifies concentrated risk. Surfaces stay flat and open, using hairlines, whitespace, optical overlap, and state changes instead of dashboard chrome.
keyCharacteristics: Pointer movement changes the model visualization directly.
One optical field carries the product mechanism.
Light paper surfaces and hairline construction keep the interface calm.
Cobalt communicates analysis; vermilion is reserved for risk concentration.
Synthetic or illustrative data is labeled wherever it could be mistaken for live output.

rules.name: The Signal Restraint Rule
rules.body: Cobalt and vermilion describe model state, not decoration. They belong in the field, selected controls, focus states, and risk conclusions—not as ambient backgrounds.

rules.name: The Analysis Before Costume Rule
rules.body: Use monospace for data and measurements, never as the default display voice.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: If depth is needed, add information or optical overlap—not a shadow.

rules.name: The Constructed Geometry Rule
rules.body: Curves live inside the analytical field; controls and reading surfaces stay sharply constructed.

dos: Do let pointer movement alter the analytical field within a bounded, useful region.
Do reserve cobalt for analysis and vermilion for concentrated risk.
Do keep synthetic data explicitly labeled.
Do use square controls, tabular measurements, and visible focus states.
Do pause shader work offscreen and preserve keyboard scenario control.
donts: Don't add neon glow, dark terminal panels, glass cards, or dashboard-card grids.
Don't use the shader as ambient decoration unrelated to portfolio state.
Don't use monospace as the display face.
Don't hide decorative canvas content without semantic text and keyboard-equivalent controls.
Don't use rounded pill containers or icons as substitutes for clear labels.
